tasks.short: Plan or supervise conservation and reclamation programmes.

steps.what: Find and assess actual industrial-site conservation or reclamation evidence
Inspect actual soil, vegetation and reclamation constraints on site
Plan feasible land conservation or reclamation methods, sequence and monitoring criteria
outputs: chosen conservation programme methods and criteria

steps.what: Write the land conservation or reclamation programme plan
inputs: chosen conservation programme methods and criteria

loop.purpose: Draft the programme description from scientist-chosen methods
loop.input: Chosen methods, actual site evidence, sequence and monitoring criteria
loop.check: Scientist checks site-specific meaning, omitted constraints, unsupported restoration promises and consistency with chosen monitoring criteria
loop.stop: Missing actual site evidence or two failed revisions returns writing to the scientist
loop.why_not_simpler: Use fixed programme fields and existing headings first; site-specific explanations vary

steps.what: Check the final conservation programme plan and its actual scope
Save the checked final conservation programme plan
Supervise actual conservation or reclamation work and assess implementation problems
Write and check actual conservation supervision findings and required follow-up
Save the checked actual conservation supervision record

tasks.design: Configure site-reference search in {DOCS} and the geographic records system {OTHER}, then use fixed plan fields before a bounded programme-description draft. The scientist inspects the site, chooses methods and checks the final plan; supervision observations and records arise only after actual authorised work occurs.
tasks.previous_blocker: Planning can repeat site-source retrieval and explanatory plan writing.
tasks.enabler_now: Native filters and bounded source-linked drafting can reduce retrieval and first-draft prose.
tasks.still_hard: Soil recovery, industrial constraints, permit interpretation and field intervention require site judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The scientist notices when a feasible written plan does not fit actual soil or implementation conditions.
tasks.altitude: Less plan preparation; land-management and supervision authority stay unchanged.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: site-reference filters and bounded plan drafting can support conservation programme records; scientific planning and physical supervision remain human.

assumptions: Planning and supervision are alternative or sequential branches. Shares describe a provisional combined workload mix; reweight to actual work rather than assuming every plan includes a supervision visit. Implementation authorisation and contractor labour belong to actual owners and have no claimed saved labour.

Site-record owners supply actual parcel identifier, survey date, soil/vegetation evidence and requirement version. The scientist assesses these in s1, observes the site in s2 and chooses methods in s3. Missing fields and sources stay manual; no site condition or supervision outcome is generated from the plan.

Test native search and fixed plan fields before code. Existing source retrieval earns no saving. Source reading stays in s1 and generated meaning correction in s4; supervision and actual outcome capture are fully retained.
Shares and reductions are provisional, not measured baselines. Each save retains its one percent share; existing final plan and record checks supply their action gates.
unknowns: What is the actual planning-versus-supervision mix?
Which site records and requirements are searchable?
research_questions: Does source-linked planning save time after all site constraints and restoration claims are checked?

incremental.description: Maintain site search filters and plan drafting checks.

approvals.approved_version: s5 checked final conservation programme plan and exact document destination; edits require recheck
s8 checked final actual conservation supervision record and exact document destination; edits require recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 15*0.30 retrieval + 14*0.30 prose = 8.7; minus 1 upkeep = 7.7. If half the retrieval and prose are eligible, 4.35 minus 1 = 3.35. Fieldwork, planning decisions, supervision and saves stay unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Research plant species for green fuels.

steps.what: Find and assess actual research on plant species and green fuel production
Choose plant species, growing conditions and fuel-production research methods
inputs: actual available plant material and facilities

steps.what: Conduct actual plant growth, biomass or conversion experiments for green fuels
Transfer and check actual plant-fuel measurements in laboratory software {OTHER}
Interpret plant species suitability and green fuel research limitations
Write and check actual plant-fuel research findings and source references
Save the checked actual plant-fuel research findings

tasks.design: Configure plant-species and conversion-topic searches in the scholarly database {OTHER}, then test native measurement imports into laboratory software {OTHER}. The scientist reads the evidence, chooses and conducts actual experiments and interprets species suitability; only source finding and numerical re-entry change.
tasks.previous_blocker: Plant-fuel research can repeat literature searches and transfer biomass or conversion measurements into analysis tables.
tasks.enabler_now: Native search filters and actual instrument import mappings can reduce retrieval and transcription.
tasks.still_hard: Agronomic performance, conversion suitability and environmental trade-offs require scientific judgement and actual evidence.
tasks.human_edge: The scientist recognises when promising laboratory fuel yield does not establish a suitable crop or production route.
tasks.altitude: Less source finding and data re-entry; research direction stays unchanged.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: scholarly saved searches and instrument imports can support plant-fuel research data handling; actual crop and conversion suitability remain scientific decisions.

assumptions: Boundary includes actual research on plant species as fuel or fuel feedstock through existing findings. Cultivation and conversion experiments are alternative methods selected by the actual research question; commercial fuel production is not inferred.

The scientist creates actual species, plot/sample, treatment and control identifiers in s2-s3; instruments supply actual mass, composition or conversion reading, timestamp and unit. The scientist verifies mapping and manually captures observations in s4. Missing exports and identifiers stay manual, with no free structured field observations.

Test native search and import configuration before custom code. Already-configured imports earn no saving; only retrieval and repeated numerical entry change, not reading, experiments or interpretation.
Shares and reductions are provisional, not measured baselines. Same-system save is one percent fully retained and uses the existing findings check.
unknowns: What measurement transfer is still manual?
Which actual research branches are used?
research_questions: Can actual biomass and conversion files be imported without losing species, sample or unit context?

incremental.description: Maintain scholarly search filters and plant-fuel measurement mappings.

approvals.approved_version: s6 checked final plant-fuel research findings and exact document destination; edits require recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 20*0.30 retrieval + 10*0.50 entry = 11; subtract 1 upkeep = 10. If half that retrieval and entry is eligible, 5.5 minus 1 = 4.5. Scientific choices, physical experiments and final findings remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Land-management and research decisions stay with the scientist while repeated source handling and plan prose can shrink.
role.ambitious_version: Formal decision rights stay unchanged; validate reduced source handling on actual conservation and fuel-research work.
